title: Without Envy
note: He has already explained envy, at couplet 35. It is the opposite of bearing wrongs, so this chapter, which forbids it, follows that one.

couplets.plain: Make it your rule of conduct to keep your heart free of envy.
couplets.pm: Take the nature free of the fault of envy in your heart as the path of conduct laid down for you. That nature also brings good, so guard it as you would conduct, above life itself.

links.quote: keep your heart free of envy
links.reason: Envy is to be kept out of the heart, as a rule of conduct.

couplets.plain: If you can be free of envy towards everyone, no great blessing equals it.
couplets.pm: If someone can get free of envy towards all, then among all the fine gains they might have, none equals that one. “Everyone” means that envy must go even towards enemies.

links.quote: free of envy towards everyone, no great blessing equals it

couplets.plain: Whoever envies another’s prosperity and won’t welcome it wants no righteousness or prosperity of their own.
couplets.pm: Someone who sees another’s wealth and turns envious, not glad, is said to want neither righteousness for the next life nor wealth for this one. Envy does harm only to the one who envies.

links.reason: Envying another’s prosperity shows a person who cares nothing for their own righteousness or prosperity.

couplets.plain: Those who know the harm a bad path brings do nothing unrighteous out of envy.
couplets.pm: The wise do nothing unrighteous because of envy, knowing that this bad path brings them suffering in both worlds. Unrighteous here means thinking, saying or doing harm against people who have wealth, learning and the like.

links.quote: do nothing unrighteous out of envy
links.reason: Those who can see the harm hold back from doing wrong through envy.

couplets.plain: Envy alone is enough for the envious. Even if their enemies fail, it brings them ruin.
couplets.pm: Envy brings ruin even where there are no enemies. So the envious need no enemies, because envy alone is enough to ruin them.

links.quote: Even if their enemies fail, it brings them ruin
links.reason: The envious need no enemy, since their own envy finishes the work.

links.quote: Envy alone is enough for the envious

couplets.plain: Whoever grudges what others are given, their kin will perish with nothing to wear and nothing to eat.
couplets.pm: Someone who envies what is given to others brings ruin on their kin, who perish without food or clothing. If the kin are ruined, that person’s own ruin needs no saying. Envy of another’s gain loses you your own gain and your kin’s as well.

couplets.plain: The red goddess of fortune cannot bear the envious. She shows them to her elder sister and goes.
couplets.pm: When someone can’t bear another’s gain, the goddess of fortune can’t bear that person either. She shows them to her elder sister and leaves. Some take அவ்வித்து to describe the envious person instead, whose mind has been made crooked.
couplets.note: செய்யவள், “the red one”, is the goddess of fortune. Her elder sister brings misfortune.

links.reason: The goddess of fortune cannot stand to stay beside the envious.

links.quote: She shows them to her elder sister and goes
links.reason: The goddess of fortune departs and shows the envious to her elder sister.

couplets.plain: That sinner called envy destroys your wealth and sends you to an evil place.
couplets.pm: The matchless sinner called envy destroys the wealth of whoever keeps it in this life and drives them to hell in the next. Envy isn’t a person, but it is called a sinner for its cruelty in ruining its owner in both worlds, as a cruel man is called a sinner.

links.reason: Personifies envy as a sinner who destroys your wealth and sends you to an evil place.

couplets.plain: When a crooked heart prospers and an upright person falls, it gives you something to think about.
couplets.pm: If someone with a heart made crooked by envy prospers, or an upright person falls, the matter is looked into. Gain and ruin can’t come from crookedness and uprightness, so the wise ask what deed from a past life lies behind them.

links.reason: The prosperity of a crooked heart is so out of order that it needs thinking about.

couplets.plain: No one has grown great through envy, and no one free of it has lost their prosperity.
couplets.pm: No one has become great by practising envy, and no one free of it has fallen from prosperity. With the last couplet, this names what brings ruin and what brings gain.

links.quote: No one has grown great through envy
links.reason: There is no case of envy raising anyone up.

links.quote: No one has grown great through envy

ideaLinks.reason: Envy itself is named as what destroys your wealth.
